name: python-exclusions
body: Python package discovery must not descend into generated, dependency, or virtual-environment trees: __pycache__, .venv, venv, .tox, .git, .hg, .mypy_cache, .pytest_cache, .ruff_cache, node_modules, site-packages, .eggs and *.egg-info are never scan roots. `site-packages` is the canonical installed-dependency tree, so it IS a never-scan-root like the rest: no file under it becomes a code node, and the Python external code-type arm therefore never matches it (requirements.requirement.python-code-type). Consistent with domain.entity.scan-exclusion (target/, vendor/, node_modules/, .worktrees/) — these are the Python-specific additions to that exclusion set. Tension with import resolution: a virtualenv / site-packages tree is excluded from discovery (never a scan root) yet the `ty` engine still resolves against it as a resolution input — it remains in the full `ty` project context (global.constraint.frontend-full-context) without being emitted; the environment model for supplying that input is an open point (requirements.note.python-frontend-open-points #3).
